specification.objective: Require explicit Hermes capability consent for model overrides on every supported host, reject stale pre-capability IPC servers, remove the Desktop scanner false positive without changing filtering, and preserve native memory safeguards. Exercise the Dashboard no-Agent fallback through the real profile-local client.

requirements.statement: The manifest declares llm.model_override and user-facing text describes capability consent and model allowlists; default-model requests remain unaffected.

A plugin-owned LLM facade forwards an explicit model only when ctx.has_capability returns True; missing or failing probes deny overrides, default-model requests remain available, and the host LLM trust/allowlist gates remain in force.
The Dashboard search filter retains its case-insensitive behavior while avoiding the !-backtick spelling that Hermes security scanning mistakes for inline shell execution.
Memory operations continue to use Hermes-native safeguards; do not replace them with direct file writes or reimplement the store. Hermes source and configuration remain unchanged.
Bump the profile IPC protocol so older active servers that do not enforce model-override capability consent are treated as incompatible and cannot receive v2 model requests.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Regression tests fail on baseline because capability is undeclared, direct/IPC model overrides pass without consent, a v1 active socket is reused, a host without a capability probe accepts an override, and Dashboard fallback can send an override; after implementation all paths fail closed while default calls and granted overrides work.
Existing executable Desktop filter tests pass and hermes plugins validate no longer reports inline_shell_exec for desktop/plugin.js.
Full CI and POLIS coverage pass without changes to Hermes source/config or native memory semantics.
A live v1 IPC listener is rejected and preserved as incompatible; v2 server/client behavior and normal IPC tests pass.

With no active Agent bridge in the Dashboard module, its ProfileLlmClient fallback reaches a capability-aware IPC server: explicit overrides fail and default-model requests succeed; test setup verifies the plugin module loaded before exercising the route.

invariants.statement: No Hermes source, Hermes configuration, credentials, or memory content is modified.

Explicit model overrides require a positive llm.model_override capability result; absent or failing capability probes never fall back to the legacy host gate, and ctx.llm trust/allowlist checks remain additional controls.
Memory reads, writes and pending approvals retain Hermes-native safeguards; no direct-write replacement is introduced.
No catalog pin update or tag is created in this change.
No IPC request reaches a legacy ungated server after the protocol version change; legacy servers fail closed until restarted.

forbidden_states.statement: An explicit model override reaches ctx.llm when capability consent is absent, denied, or cannot be checked.
The filter refactor changes search results or removes the documented Desktop SDK integration.
Hermes source, user config, or memory is changed.
A profile IPC listener using the old protocol is accepted as compatible or receives a model override request.

inputs.statement: Current Hermes validators pass but report missing capability declaration, private core imports, and an inline-shell false positive.
Current Hermes PluginContext exposes has_capability and ctx.llm enforces the legacy model-override trust gate.
No documented public PluginContext API was found for reading built-in memory state or applying native pending-memory decisions; these operations must not be reimplemented unsafely.
The existing IPC protocol version is reused by old servers that forward model= directly to ctx.llm, bypassing the new capability-aware wrapper after an in-place plugin update.
The plugin minimum Hermes version includes hosts without ctx.has_capability; explicit override behavior must fail closed on those hosts while default-model requests remain supported.

outputs.statement: Plugin-only capability declaration/check, versioned IPC compatibility boundary, and Desktop scanner-warning cleanup, with old hosts failing closed for explicit overrides and the Hermes public memory API gap reported.

failure_semantics.statement: If ctx.has_capability is absent, raises, or denies, the configured model is not forwarded; default-model calls still use ctx.llm.
If removing private core imports requires undocumented memory APIs or bypasses native transactions, stop and report the upstream API blocker.
If an older protocol server is already active, new plugin instances reject it and requests fail safely until the Agent plugin is restarted; the old server is not removed.
